text:
emily_cs: FYI, ACCT-1234 reported that after they applied a promo code and upgraded from trial -> paid, their free-tier credits were drained before promo credits. Dashboard shows 0 free credits remaining, but promo credit balance on invoice is >0. They say this started after yesterday's deploy. :frowning:

jordan_support: thanks — can you paste the account id + example request ids? also which promo code?

emily_cs: account acct_1234. Example request ids: req_8a1f2, req_8a1f3, req_8a2b01. Promo code is SUMMER2026. Customer timeline: 2026-02-27 18:02 applied promo, 18:03 made a batch of generation calls (~25 short requests). Dashboard realtime shows free_credits -> 0 at 18:03. Billing ledger shows promo_credit.balance 600 -> should've been consumed first per policy.

mike_billing: putting in quick logs — I see allocation job ran at 18:02:15 and gave promo_credit:600. Billing consumer processed requests at 18:03:01..18:03:20 and the ledger entries show token_charge.source=free_tier for req_8a1f2 and req_8a1f3. That's suspect. Possibly ordering issue in credits service.

sara_sre: could be a race between promo-apply webhook and the token-usage consumer. Repro suggestion: apply a promo and immediately fire concurrent requests. I can try a local repro with a script to hammer the /v1/generate endpoint after applying promo.

jordan_support: actionable for now: 1) ask customer to suspend traffic and we can revert charges if confirmed, 2) collect traces for the example req ids, 3) escalate to eng-billing.

emily_cs: Customer agreed to pause traffic. They provided the request payload for req_8a1f2:
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-small-1",
  "input": "Summarize...",
  "max_tokens": 16
}
```
Trace header they sent: X-Trace-Id: trace-20260227-8a1f2

mike_billing: grabbed the trace (trace-20260227-8a1f2). In the trace span sequence I see: 1) credits-service.apply_promo (18:02:15.123) 2) credits-service.cache_invalidate (18:02:15.125) 3) routing-layer.forward (18:03:01.004) 4) usage-processor.consume (18:03:01.006) -> token_charge.with_source=free_tier. The apply_promo completed before the usage, but cache invalidation may be eventually consistent. Looks like usage-processor read a stale cache entry.

billing-bot: Invoice snapshot created for acct_1234 — invoice_2026-02-28 (amount: $12.34). Promo credit applied: 600 units. Free tier credit usage recorded: 350 units. Promo usage recorded: 0 units.

sara_sre: likely root cause: usage-processor reads credits via credits-cache which is updated asynchronously. If cache still returned old balance (no promo) usage goes to free_tier. Fix options: 1) make credits lookup strongly consistent for immediate post-promo calls, 2) change usage-processor to re-check pending promo application when it sees an account-level flag. Quick mitigation: add a short delay in promo-apply path to populate cache before returning (risky).

mike_billing: I can implement a conservative fix: when promo-apply returns success add a tombstone version bump to cache and publish a sync event; usage-processor will prefer on-disk ledger if cache version mismatch. Will submit PR, but timeline ~2 business days.

jordan_support: next steps for support: 1) open billing adjust ticket to credit back 350 free-tier tokens consumed erroneously, 2) attach traces + ledger snapshot, 3) tag eng-billing and eng-sre. I've created ticket #CS-8721 and assigned to @mike_billing and @sara_sre.

emily_cs: customer accepted credit adjustment and wants ETA — gave them "fix in ~48 hours + retroactive credit now". Marking this thread for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
